newsitem.title: USA: Morgan trader dismisses heatoil squeeze talk.
newsitem.headline: Morgan trader dismisses heatoil squeeze talk.

text.p: Morgan Stanley is not hoarding heating oil in the New York Harbor market in an effort to drive prices higher, according to a trader at the Wall Street brokerage.

He confirmed that Morgan Stanley took delivery on about a 500,000 barrels in heating oil on the April New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) contract, which expired on March 31, and that the firm settled for cash on a smaller April position.
However, he said Morgan Stanley had recently been a willing seller in the cash market.
"A 'squeeze' is only if you refuse to sell. Every party that has called us we have sold to. We have not refused to sell to a single party," said the trader, who asked not to be quoted by name.
"In fact, we have been the best offer in the (New York) Harbor every day," he added.
The New York Harbor and the U.S. Gulf are the two major U.S. cash markets for heating oil.

"We always have requirement for No. 2 oil (heating oil). We do sizeable New York volume," he said, explaining that the size of the April delivery is fairly typical and was meant to supply Morgan Stanley's wholesale and retail operation in New Haven, Connecticut.
The talk of the squeeze comes at a time when an unseasonal cold snap in the northeastern United States is lifting heating oil prices. The region is the largest heating oil market in the world.
"What we have is a situation with a 10-day period of cold weather that was unexpected. My luck," the Morgan trader said.
The talk that Morgan was "squeezing" the market may have stemmed in part from its history of sometimes taking particularly large heating oil deliveries when many in the market were selling "short."
Last August, for example, the firm took delivery of three million barrels when heating oil supply was at record low levels in New England.
At that time, the price of the spot heating oil contract jumped two cents, or about four percent, in the sessions leading up to the delivery.
A number of other firms have followed a similar strategy.

At 1342 EDT, May heating oil was up 0.44 cent a gallon at 53.55 cents while May crude was off a penny at $19.25 a barrel. May heating oil has risen 0.55 cent a gallon since Monday while May crude has lost 29 cents a barrel in that time.
